title: One Silk Thread, Split 48 Ways, Hides Two Pictures | China Travel Expert
description:
One strand of silk, split as fine as 48 filaments — then embroidered into two different pictures on a single sheet of sheer silk.

This is Suzhou double-sided embroidery (苏绣双面绣), one of China's four great embroidery traditions. A master splits a single silk thread into up to 48 finer strands and works both faces of one translucent silk panel — so each side shows a completely different image, stitched from the same side while holding both pictures in mind at once. Su embroidery has been practiced around Suzhou for well over 1,000 years.

🧭 Expert Tip: To watch it done by hand, visit the Suzhou Embroidery Museum or the workshops of Zhenhu, the craft's home town on Suzhou's western edge.

一根丝线劈成48丝，一片薄绢，两面绣出两幅不同的画。
